strings.en:
...frustrations with Dr. Flintock have only increased as we argue about the location of this supposed hidden dungeon, but I finally persuaded him that southward was the best heading...

***

...Today, as we set up camp, we noticed frightened families hastening northward. Said something about a storm—some even called it "dark spirits." I couldn't help sharing a smile with Flintock. These people are definitely spiritual, with all the credulity that accompanies it. And it was at that precise moment that I recognized the coastline. Exactly the same as on the map. We are practically on top of it!

***

...Flintock is dead! I leave now to save myself from...I don't know what! An evil... It gets inside you. His ashen face looked at me, gnarled and anguished. Then came the calmest whisper from him, "Join us in the enveloping darkness, and we will be as one."

And then what he breathed out... Black as coal dust, but it moved like tentacles.

Let my last message be a warning. GET OUT OF THIS AREA NOW! Head north and...

strings.en:
It is with considerable excitement that we await the results of our joint venture, Director. Now more than ever, it is vital that we reinforce this council and the asuran people for the journey ahead. The artifacts and technology that you will bring back to us will form the foundation for a new golden age.  
  
We must remind you, of course, to honor the terms of our agreement and bring your findings back only to Rata Sum. We have, after all, invested significant capital in your equipment and provisions. In return, we will ensure that any impediments to your expedition are prevented or significantly delayed.  
  
We look forward to an update on your findings.  
  
(The bottom of the page is marked with the official seal of the Arcane Council.)

Captain,  

Normally I'd bend your ear over a sea shanty and a keg, but with you being in Lion's Arch on assignment I figured I'd put it to paper. I'll give it to you straight, Mai—I don't like the current arrangement. I yearn for a good scrap and a rousing adventure as much as the next pirate, but the new boss is an anchor that's pulling us down. Mark my words, we're getting tangled in a mess and we won't notice 'til it chokes us out.  

Then there's the Inquest buggers. Can't argue with the upgrades to our airships and equipment, but they're not like us. Got no code.  

Goes without saying that I'll follow you to a cold and briny grave a thousand times over, but I want it to be on our terms—doing what we love, our freedom above all else. No fat-cat life for this first mate, you hear?  

F.M. Horrik  

P.S. Speaking of fat cats, threw half a fish to a stray the other day. Wouldn't mind having one on the ship. I know you like them.

### Skippy & the Sailor
"Meow," said Skippy.

What he meant by this was, "I love treats and blankets, as you do! I accept the position of cabin boy on this fateful journey from Cat Storah to Tear Eeyuh!"

Leo rejoiced.

"I look forward to observing your sailing prowess, my captain!" added Skippy.

That's when Leo realized he needed a sailor.

"I need a sailor!" exclaimed Leo.

Skippy said, "Shenanigans!"

Leo's whiskers twitched in confusion.

"Shenanigans is her name, Leo! She's white as a sail herself and loves the view of the waves from her perch to the north in the arches!"

"Meow!" cried Leo determinedly, and off they trotted.

strings.en: You have typed characters that Guild Wars 2 does not currently support. We're sorry for the inconvenience.

I've been tracking the non-dredge allied members of the Flame Legion, as requested. It doesn't look like all of them are on board with this...thing. Whatever it is.  
  
Tribune Efram Greetsglory is especially outspoken about his disapproval. He's been moving a lot on his own. I followed him out of their camp the other night—had a younger cub with him. They traveled to the edge of Buloh Crossing to meet with someone. Charr. Didn't recognize their face, but they didn't look like Flame Legion either. I couldn't get close enough to hear what they were talking about, but they both seemed uneasy.  
  
The other charr took off with the cub, and Efram returned to camp. Hasn't left since, but I've got eyes on him. Trying to figure out the cub's identity and location, too. I think they went further north.  
  
I'll let you know if anything suspect happens. I'm meeting with Crecia Stoneglow in two moons—maybe leave that part out of your report to Rytlock. I'll include any intel she has for us.  
  
Morva Baeldancer

Hypothesis: High Kryptis and Low Kryptis possess differing internal biological systems resulting in the High Kryptis's increased size and strength.  
  
Principals: Research Lead Simma (Natural), Research Assistant Toft (Knowledge)  
  
Methodology: Comparison of Kryptis biological systems via autopsy of varied High and Low specimens, employing a team of cross-bastion volunteers participating in corpse acquisition, dismemberment, organ processing, and analysis.  
  
Findings: We discovered no disparities among similar/related species in High/Low Kryptis biological systems aside from standard deviations related to overall structure or musculature.  
  
Conclusion: Hypothesis unsupported.  
  
Research in progress (tentative; pending further autopsies, interrogations, and exploration):  
  
—Part II: Feeding Patterns, Dietary Habits, and Their Relation to Kryptis Stature  
—Part III: The Effect of Cultural and Societal Factors on Kryptis Size and Strength  
—Part IV: The Impact of Lineage and Pedigree on Kryptis Power Potential

To: All Research Staff
RE: Let's get inspired!

Many of you attended the quarterly address by our illustrious director. For those who missed it, I recommend a holographic viewing; it covered important ground regarding workplace culture. In short, his message was that grand plans and world-changing ambitions aren't only about glory. We should all reflect on important virtues that are too often overlooked: hard work, personal sacrifice, and humility.

Please note that this message does not imply any reduced emphasis on productivity or outcomes. Researchers unable to produce results in the lab will continue to be subject to the usual hierarchy of punitive actions.

Have a productive quarter!
